overview: Build the UI as ONE governed responsive layer, outside-in in the canonical order (ScreenGui -> root container Frame -> layout/constraint objects -> content -> styling -> script), never element-by-element. Every GUI object is made with create_instance and configured with set_property; all scripting (TweenService feedback, runtime-cloned templates, a ViewportSize-keyed UIScale, a central style ModuleScript, reactive data) goes through run_luau; capture/capture_angles + evaluate(category='gui') close the loop. The four moves that separate this from a generic 'AI did it' UI: (1) Scale-not-Offset sizing under one governed root, (2) layout objects own all placement and spacing, (3) a centralized role-based palette + type scale + token system, and (4) TweenService micro-feedback wired as a system that reaches runtime-spawned elements.

killer_systems.name: Governed responsive Scale layer
killer_systems.what: The whole UI is reasoned about as ONE responsive layer whose scaling/anchoring is owned in a single place: a transparent full-screen root Frame (BackgroundTransparency=1) under the ScreenGui, with Size/Position in UDim2 Scale and role-matched AnchorPoint, so children inherit the layer's responsive behavior instead of each carrying an absolute pixel position. Optionally a single ViewportSize-keyed UIScale governs the entire subtree.
killer_systems.how: create_instance a ScreenGui under StarterGui (ResetOnSpawn=false for HUD, ScreenInsets=CoreUISafeInsets, DisplayOrder for modals). create_instance a root Frame child; set_property BackgroundTransparency=1, AnchorPoint={0.5,0.5}, Position=UDim2.fromScale(0.5,0.5), Size in Scale. For the one-scaler substrate, run_luau to insert a UIScale and set UIScale.Scale = 1/math.max(base.X/viewport.X, base.Y/viewport.Y) recomputed on Camera:GetPropertyChangedSignal('ViewportSize'). All later elements are children of this root and use Scale Size/Position with Offset reserved only for UIStroke thickness and small crisp icons.

killer_systems.name: Layout-driven composition
killer_systems.what: Repeated/structured arrangements (HUD rows, menus, shop grids, inventory cells, settings lists) are produced declaratively by layout objects (UIListLayout / UIGridLayout / UITableLayout), never by hand-positioning each sibling, so spacing stays uniform and the design survives adding/removing items. Inner margins (UIPadding) are distinguished from between-item gutters (layout Padding), with one repeated padding value.
killer_systems.how: create_instance a UIListLayout (or UIGridLayout) as a child of each container; set_property FillDirection, SortOrder=LayoutOrder, Padding (a UDim gap BETWEEN items), HorizontalAlignment/VerticalAlignment. Give each child a LayoutOrder integer; leave child Position untouched (the layout overrides it). create_instance a separate UIPadding inside each container for the OUTER margin (UIListLayout.Padding does not pad the list's outer bounds). For grids, set CellSize/CellPadding; for tabular rows use UITableLayout.

killer_systems.name: Centralized design system (tokens)
killer_systems.what: A single source of style truth: ~4-5 role-named colors (base, background-2, outline, text, one reserved accent for CTAs), a 2-3 tier type scale (header/subhead/body size+weight in ONE clean family like Gotham), and one repeated spacing value — defined once and reused everywhere, ideally with meaning-bearing concepts (Health, currency, rarity) locked to fixed colors and monochrome icons recolored via ImageColor3. At full strength a StyleSheet of StyleRules with $-tokens + Themes, or reusable component templates whose style is defined once.
killer_systems.how: run_luau to create a ModuleScript (Theme/Tokens) in ReplicatedStorage returning a table of role colors + type scale + spacing. Reference those tokens when set_property sets BackgroundColor3/TextColor3/Font/TextSize on each element rather than picking values per element. Primary buttons = filled accent; secondary = muted/gray/text-only. For the exceptional path, create_instance a StyleSheet with StyleRule children using selectors + $tokens + Theme objects, or define one reusable component template cloned per use.

killer_systems.name: TweenService feedback system
killer_systems.what: Every interactive element acknowledges input through TweenService-driven micro-feedback — a snappy hover (scale-up via a child UIScale and/or UIStroke 0->2-3px + brightness) and a quick press scale-down that settles — and state changes are animated (panels start off-screen+Visible and tween in), not hard-cut. Crucially this is wired as a SYSTEM that auto-applies to runtime-spawned elements (a PlayerGui.DescendantAdded linker, or feedback baked into reusable component templates) and is bound to the cross-platform Activated event.
killer_systems.how: run_luau: build a feedback module that, on MouseEnter, plays TweenService:Create(childUIScale, TweenInfo.new(0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {Scale=1.08}):Play(), tweens back on MouseLeave, scales down on press. Drive scale via a child UIScale (not Size) so layout siblings don't fight it; AnchorPoint {0.5,0.5} so it grows from center. Connect a PlayerGui.DescendantAdded listener that attaches the feedback to any new GuiButton, and bind clicks to button.Activated (mouse/touch/gamepad). Animate open/close by pre-setting the frame off-screen and tweening Position; add a Lighting blur on modal open.

common_pitfalls: Parenting content straight to the ScreenGui with no root container Frame: the whole screen can't be moved/scaled as a unit and layout grouping breaks. Always insert one transparent full-screen root Frame (BackgroundTransparency=1) first; forgetting that transparency leaves opaque gray boxes everywhere.

Leaving inserted elements at the engine defaults — pixel Offset Size/Position and AnchorPoint 0,0. This is the #1 'looks fine on PC, squished/overflowing on mobile' tell. Set AnchorPoint by role BEFORE positioning, then use UDim2 Scale; reserve Offset for UIStroke thickness and small crisp icons only.

Hand-positioning siblings instead of letting a layout object own placement. A UIListLayout/UIGridLayout OVERRIDES each child's Position, so manual nudges silently do nothing and adding one item breaks alignment. Set SortOrder=LayoutOrder + per-child LayoutOrder.

Confusing the two spacing systems: UIPadding is the container's INNER margin; layout Padding is the gap BETWEEN items. UIListLayout.Padding does NOT pad the list's outer bounds — you need a separate UIPadding for that.

A constraint (UIAspectRatioConstraint / UISizeConstraint) on a child OVERRIDES the layout's sizing of that child — place constraints at the governing container level, not stamped on every child, or they fight the layout.

Scale-based CellSize or Scale layout Padding inside a ScrollingFrame with AutomaticCanvasSize creates a circular dependency / corrupts the measurement so items vanish or get cut off; use Offset CellSize and Offset padding in scrollable content, and set VerticalScrollBarInset so the last row isn't hidden under the bar.

Tweening Size directly on a layout-driven child (fights the layout) or tweening UIStroke.Thickness on text (re-rasterizes glyphs every frame, flicker + perf hit). Tween a child UIScale instead, and use LineJoinMode=Bevel/Miter on thick text strokes.

Ad-hoc per-element color (rainbow) and a wall of identical bright buttons: without a reserved accent the accent stops meaning 'click here'. Define the palette once centrally and differentiate primary (filled accent) vs secondary (muted) buttons.
Pure black/white tones and hue-only contrast: use off-black (~35,35,35) backgrounds and off-white text, build separation on value+saturation (survives colorblindness), never red/green-only signaling.

Ignoring platform chrome: buttons under the ~58px top bar / notch / bottom joystick+jump button, touch targets under ~44-50px, and ResetOnSpawn left at true (silently wipes runtime HUD state on respawn). Design mobile-first and verify in the Device Emulator via capture.

Hand-toggled Visible flags that blink, and feedback wired only to load-time buttons via mouse-only MouseButton1Click: animate transitions, and wire feedback as a DescendantAdded/component system bound to Activated so runtime-spawned cards behave identically.

tiers.goal: One governed responsive layer that re-proportions with the viewport: a transparent full-screen root Frame under the ScreenGui, every element Scale-sized with a role-matched AnchorPoint, repeated arrangements owned by layout objects with systematic padding, and a central role-based palette — clearing the architecture-level tells (Offset-on-my-monitor, hand-placed siblings, cramped borders, rainbow color) before any decoration.

steps.instruction: create_instance a ScreenGui under StarterGui named by function (e.g. HUDGui, ShopGui); set_property ZIndexBehavior=Sibling, ResetOnSpawn=false for persistent HUD, and DisplayOrder (multiples of 100) so modals layer above the HUD. Then create_instance ONE root container Frame as its child and set_property BackgroundTransparency=1 (transparent so it's an invisible governing layer), AnchorPoint={0.5,0.5}, Position=UDim2.fromScale(0.5,0.5), Size in Scale. All other UI becomes children of this root so the whole layer is positioned/scaled once and children inherit it.
steps.pitfalls: Parenting content straight to the ScreenGui (no root Frame) makes the screen impossible to move/scale as a unit and breaks grouping; forgetting BackgroundTransparency=1 leaves an opaque gray box covering the screen. ResetOnSpawn defaults to true and silently re-clones the HUD on every respawn, wiping runtime state.

steps.instruction: For every element, set_property AnchorPoint FIRST by on-screen role (0.5,0.5 centered panel; 1,1 bottom-right currency; 0,0 top-left label), THEN set Position and Size with UDim2 Scale (e.g. UDim2.fromScale(0.5,0.5) position, Scale Size like {0.4,0},{0.6,0}). Confine Offset to genuinely non-scaling things (UIStroke thickness, small crisp icons). This pairing makes elements grow from the correct origin and hold proportions across phone/tablet/desktop.
steps.pitfalls: Inserted Roblox UI defaults to Offset and AnchorPoint 0,0 — the #1 mobile-overflow tell. Mismatching AnchorPoint and Position (anchor 0,0 but trying to center) drifts elements off-screen at other resolutions; mixing Offset Position with Scale Size looks fine in Studio but misaligns on phones. Scale alone still distorts on portrait/ultrawide — add the aspect constraint in the good tier.

steps.instruction: For any repeated/structured arrangement (HUD rows, menus, shop grids, inventory cells, settings lists), create_instance a layout object as a child of the container instead of hand-positioning siblings: UIListLayout for rows/columns (set_property FillDirection, SortOrder=LayoutOrder, Padding for the inter-item gap, HorizontalAlignment/VerticalAlignment), UIGridLayout for uniform cells (CellSize, CellPadding, FillDirectionMaxCells), UITableLayout for tabular rows. Give each child a LayoutOrder integer and leave its Position untouched.
steps.pitfalls: A layout object OVERRIDES each sibling's Position (and influences Size), so manual Position nudges silently do nothing. Leaving SortOrder at the default makes runtime-cloned items appear unpredictably — always SortOrder=LayoutOrder + per-child LayoutOrder. A UISizeConstraint/UIAspectRatioConstraint on a child overrides the layout's sizing of that child.

steps.instruction: create_instance a UIPadding inside every card/button/list container and set_property PaddingTop/Bottom/Left/Right to ONE repeated value (e.g. a Scale UDim, or UDim.new(0,8)) so content never sits flush to the frame edges — this is the inner margin. Keep the gap BETWEEN items on the layout object's Padding (UIListLayout.Padding / UIGridLayout.CellPadding), distinct from the container margin. Reuse the same padding measurement everywhere so spacing reads as systematic, and use extra whitespace deliberately to emphasize an element.
steps.pitfalls: Content jammed against borders is the most common 'cramped' note. UIListLayout.Padding pads only BETWEEN items, not the list's outer bounds — you still need a separate container UIPadding. Conflating inner margins with inter-item gutters makes spacing look ad-hoc. Inside a ScrollingFrame, Scale padding corrupts AutomaticCanvasSize — use Offset there.

steps.instruction: Before styling, run_luau to create a central style source — a ModuleScript (Theme/Tokens) in ReplicatedStorage returning ~4-5 role-named colors (base, background-2, outline, text, ONE reserved accent for CTAs) plus the type scale and one spacing value — OR store the roles in a Configuration object. Then when you set_property BackgroundColor3/TextColor3 on each element, pull from those roles rather than picking colors per element. Make primary buttons filled-accent and secondary buttons muted/gray/text-only so not every button is equally loud.
steps.pitfalls: Ad-hoc per-element ('rainbow') color and a wall of identical bright buttons are the loudest amateur signals and cause misclicks; without a reserved accent the accent stops meaning 'click here'. If colors aren't centralized, a re-skin means editing every element by hand.

tiers.goal: Above-the-mean polish: container-level constraints that hold shape and clamp extremes, text/content that scales with the layout, content-derived scrolling lists from cloned templates, animated multi-view switching, a disciplined type + semantic-color + depth/material design system, mobile-first safe areas and touch targets, gestalt grouping and progressive disclosure, tactile buttons, and the known corner/stroke render fixes — all from a structure-first workflow.

steps.instruction: create_instance constraint objects at the CONTAINER level (not stamped on every child): a UIAspectRatioConstraint on each governing panel/card frame (set_property AspectRatio) to lock shape so Scale-sized frames never skew on iPads/ultrawide; a UISizeConstraint (MinSize/MaxSize) to clamp elements so buttons stay tappable on phones and not absurd on 4K; and a UITextSizeConstraint (MinTextSize >= 9, MaxTextSize) to keep auto-scaled text legible. Drive UICorner radius with Scale, not Offset.
steps.pitfalls: A constraint on an element under a layout OVERRIDES the layout's control of that element's size — place constraints deliberately at the governing frame, not on every child (over-constraining every child is a 'big mess'). Never set MinTextSize below 9. Pair a UIAspectRatioConstraint with AnchorPoint {0.5,0.5} since it can shift apparent position.

steps.instruction: Tie text into the responsive system so it doesn't stay one frozen size while the layout scales: set_property TextScaled=true on labels (clamped by the UITextSizeConstraint from the previous step) so text resizes with its container, AND set_property AutomaticSize=Y (or XY) with TextWrapped on boxes holding variable/localized strings so they grow to fit. Remember Size becomes the MINIMUM and the box grows from its AnchorPoint.
steps.pitfalls: 'Everything scales except the text' (one frozen TextSize on a scaling layout) is the #1 device-correctness tell. AutomaticSize in the same axis a parent UIListLayout fills acts as a flex basis rather than a hard size; AutomaticSize + Scale Size on the same axis conflict. If you adopt a single ViewportSize-keyed UIScale later, drop TextScaled (fixed TextSize scales cleanly with the UIScale; TextScaled competes).

steps.instruction: For variable-length lists/grids (inventories, leaderboards, shop rows, settings), create_instance a ScrollingFrame containing a UIListLayout/UIGridLayout, then run_luau to clone ONE reusable item-template Frame per data entry (set its LayoutOrder + content, parent into the layout). Make the scroll extent content-derived: set_property AutomaticCanvasSize=Y (or bind CanvasSize to the layout's AbsoluteContentSize via GetPropertyChangedSignal) so the canvas grows/shrinks with the item set and survives add/remove. set_property VerticalScrollBarInset=ScrollBar so content isn't hidden under the bar.
steps.pitfalls: Hard-setting CanvasSize breaks the first time the item count changes. Scale-based layout Padding or Scale CellSize inside a ScrollingFrame corrupts the AutomaticCanvasSize measurement (children get excluded) — use Offset padding/CellSize in scrollable content. Forgetting VerticalScrollBarInset hides the last row/column under the scrollbar.

steps.instruction: Switch between panels/screens/tabs (settings categories, shop pages, menu views) through a systematized, ANIMATED mechanism, not hand-toggled Visible flags: create_instance a UIPageLayout in the holder frame with each page a sibling Frame (set_property Animated=true, EasingStyle, EasingDirection, TweenTime, optionally Circular), OR run_luau to drive reusable templated panels whose open/close/switch is one tweened operation. Add an inner UIPadding so pages center without the next page peeking at the edge.
steps.pitfalls: Hand-toggled Visible flags blink in/out (the 'made in 10 minutes' tell). Without inner page UIPadding the adjacent UIPageLayout page peeks at the edge — bump the padding to clip it. A single static screen with no transitions fails this criterion outright.

steps.instruction: Establish a 2-3 tier header/subhead/body hierarchy through SIZE and WEIGHT within ONE clean non-decorative family (Gotham in-engine): run_luau or set_property FontFace/Font + TextSize from the type scale in your tokens module (bold headers carrying scannable info, lighter body). Keep to 2-3 text colors. In rows, set_property TextXAlignment so labels are Left and values are Right (the clean-row pattern), and de-emphasize secondary text with TextTransparency ~0.1 rather than shrinking it into illegibility.
steps.pitfalls: One undifferentiated text size everywhere, or mixed/decorative/Legacy fonts, is an instant amateur tell and leaves the screen unscannable. Left-stacking every row (no label-left/value-right) reads as haphazard. Shrinking secondary text into illegibility (vs ~0.1 TextTransparency) destroys hierarchy.

steps.instruction: Reuse the defined-once palette from the tokens module systematically across the WHOLE UI (a single source of color truth), and lock meaning-bearing concepts (Health, each currency, rarity) to a fixed color repeated on that concept's text + icon + bar everywhere it appears — set_property the same Color3 from the token wherever the concept shows. Make the palette/mood a deliberate, genre-matched choice (playful sim -> bright/high-chroma; serious/competitive -> restrained dark), not an engine-reflex gray/white default.
steps.pitfalls: Default gray/white or per-screen ad-hoc color carries no consistency. A concept whose color drifts between its text, icon, and bar reads as careless. Shipping a generic look regardless of the game (no stated genre->palette reasoning) only reaches partial — state the emotional tone first, then pull the palette to match.

steps.instruction: Give every panel/button authored material instead of flat square rectangles: create_instance a UICorner (set CornerRadius with a Scale UDim) PLUS at least one deliberate depth layer — a thin semi-transparent UIStroke (border, dark not white), a soft drop-shadow ImageLabel placed BEHIND the frame, and/or a subtle top-down UIGradient (lighter at top). For focal surfaces, escape the default square primitive with custom transparent-PNG art via an ImageLabel/ImageButton (white-base so ImageColor3/UIGradient recolors per theme/state). Apply the rounded/styled treatment consistently across surfaces.
steps.pitfalls: Flat single-color frames with square corners are the clearest 'AI did it' surface; white outlines wash out edges (use a darkened version of the fill color). Avoid shadows ON icons and strokes on bare text. A fixed-Offset UICorner radius won't scale with a responsive layout — use Scale. For nested rounded boxes set outer radius = inner radius + padding so corners stay concentric.

steps.instruction: Draw repeated small visual elements (icons, indicators, status glyphs, button glyphs) as ONE unified family governed centrally: create_instance ImageLabels/ImageButtons using a single consistent monochrome (white-base) icon style and set_property ImageColor3 from the palette so a hover/selected/disabled state is one tint change. Load icons via the rbxassetid:// string in the Image property. Drive every icon's color from the design system rather than shipping mismatched, multicolor, or default-gray glyphs.
steps.pitfalls: Mismatched/default-gray/ungoverned glyphs read as unfinished. Assigning a bare numeric ID (or an http URL) to Image silently fails to load — use the full 'rbxassetid://NUMBER' string. ImageTransparency (the picture) and BackgroundTransparency (the box) are different properties.

steps.instruction: Engineer text/background contrast for legibility and accessibility: set_property off-black backgrounds (~Color3.fromRGB(35,35,35)) and off-white text — never pure #000/#FFF — and build element separation on VALUE (lightness) + SATURATION rather than hue alone so it survives colorblindness (~1 in 12 men). Never rely on red/green-only signaling. Verify text/background pairs against a contrast checker.
steps.pitfalls: Pure black-on-white causes eye strain and pure-black panels read cheap; hue-only 'orange on blue' contrast vibrates and collapses for colorblind players. Shrinking secondary text into illegibility (instead of ~0.1 TextTransparency) destroys hierarchy.

steps.instruction: Design the HUD mobile-first: set_property ScreenGui.ScreenInsets=CoreUISafeInsets (DeviceSafeInsets for notch-only) so descendants clear the Roblox top bar and screen cutouts, keep interactive elements clear of the ~58px top bar / chat / leaderboard and the bottom-left joystick + bottom-right jump button, and size touch targets ~44-50px minimum (~0.06 scale). Layer modals via DisplayOrder, keep persistent HUD ResetOnSpawn=false. run_luau GuiService:GetGuiInset() when positioning by code, and capture/capture_angles in the Device Emulator to verify on a notched phone.
steps.pitfalls: Ignoring the topbar/notch and mobile control zones puts buttons under the jump button or crops them behind a notch. IgnoreGuiInset pushes UI under the top bar — only for full-bleed backgrounds, never interactive elements. Touch targets under ~44px are untappable on phones.

steps.instruction: Impose readable structure on dense screens: cluster related items tightly in their own sub-frames (each with its own layout + tighter Padding) and separate unrelated groups with larger whitespace gutters, so categories read by proximity without labels. Then triage real estate via progressive disclosure — surface only the 3-5 controls relevant to the current context and defer the rest behind the tabs/scrolling/collapsible panels you already built, swapping action sets by game state via run_luau — instead of dumping every control on one static screen.
steps.pitfalls: One even grid with uniform gaps across unrelated items makes unrelated things look related (gestalt fail). Dumping every control on a permanent static screen overloads the player. Separating groups by space alone (without shared visual treatment) reads only partly.

steps.instruction: Build each button as a physical, pressable object: a colored container (distinct from the background, rounded via UICorner, bold centered text) holding the label/icon, with a soft drop shadow BELOW and a subtle lighter top-edge highlight so it reads as raised — and expand the clickable region to the whole button/row. Reuse platform conventions for muscle memory: an X close button top-right, conventional dismiss. Wire clicks via button.Activated in run_luau.
steps.pitfalls: Bare TextButtons / single-flat-color rectangles don't read as clickable, and novelty controls in odd places force relearning. A tiny inner hit target (vs the whole row) is hard to tap on phones.

steps.instruction: Anticipate and solve the known rounded-corner/stroke render artifacts where the relevant elements exist: for thick text strokes set_property UIStroke.LineJoinMode=Bevel (or Miter) so letters don't show through at high thickness; for a rounded progress/health bar, create_instance a CanvasGroup as the bar background (ClipsDescendants is on by default) and parent the fill bar inside it so the rounded fill is clipped and doesn't poke past the UICorner'd background at low values.
steps.pitfalls: Default UIStroke LineJoinMode=Round causes visible overlap/see-through where letters meet at high thickness. A naked UICorner on a shrinking bar bugs out and doesn't fit the background at small values — the CanvasGroup's clipping is the fix.

steps.instruction: Work structure-first, not element-by-element: before decorating, establish the hierarchy/layout and lock one consistent style up front. create_instance the grayscale region-zoning blockout (objectives top, gameplay center, controls in thumb zones) and/or lock the style on one sample frame, then propagate it across all frames via the layout objects and reusable templates already chosen — so the result is a coherent skeleton rather than elements placed one at a time. (Optionally mock the whole UI in an external editor first to lock one visual language.)
steps.pitfalls: Decorating first and structuring never (ad-hoc absolute placement) is exactly what a beginner ships. Hand-styling each element independently is why pieces clash — lock and propagate one style instead.

tiers.goal: Design-system-grade craft: layout-distributed flex space, a single multi-axis focal point, centralized style tokens/StyleSheet, an elevation/shadow system, scale-aware 9-slice surfaces, TweenService feedback wired as a system to runtime-spawned elements with a tone-matched easing personality, RichText inline emphasis, a reusable prop/state component architecture, presentation/data separation, and a header/body/footer composition that steers the eye.

steps.instruction: Let the layout system distribute leftover space instead of hand-coded pixel gaps: on a UIListLayout set_property HorizontalFlex/VerticalFlex=Fill for equal-width tabs (or SpaceBetween/SpaceAround/SpaceEvenly), and/or create_instance a UIFlexItem on specific children (FlexMode=Grow/Fill/Shrink) to act as a spacer or grow a child — so nav strips fill the width and items space evenly under resize. At minimum, drive every inter-item gap from the layout object's Padding/alignment so spacing reflows on resize.
steps.pitfalls: Faking even spacing with fixed pixel gaps breaks on resize. Flex + wrapping add per-frame layout cost — don't enable flex on huge dynamic lists you rebuild every frame. AutomaticSize interacts with flex as 'automatic flex basis', changing how sizes resolve.

steps.instruction: Make ONE element win the eye by stacking MULTIPLE emphasis signals on it at once while muting the rest: pick the single featured element (primary CTA, featured gamepass, top bundle) and set_property to give it larger area AND brighter/more-saturated color (from the accent role) AND extra surrounding whitespace (a larger UIPadding) AND a distinguishing accent stripe/badge (an extra create_instance'd Frame/ImageLabel) — while deliberately de-emphasizing peers' size and color, so the eye lands where you chose.
steps.pitfalls: A flat grid where every card/button has equal size/color/weight gives the eye nowhere to land (the single biggest tell of unintentional design). Emphasizing on only one axis (just bigger, or just a different color) leads weakly — stack 2+ axes.

steps.instruction: Centralize all visual design so a restyle is a single change: create_instance a StyleSheet with StyleRule children using selectors + $-tokens + Theme objects (light/dark), OR run_luau to build a code-side token/component system — reusable component templates whose style is defined once in the tokens module and propagated — so colors/corners/spacing live in one place. Changing the look becomes one edit, not per-instance copy-paste.
steps.pitfalls: Copy-pasting identical (or default) properties onto every instance makes restyling a manual slog and themes impossible. A partial token table with many properties still per-instance only reaches partial.

steps.instruction: Make depth a consistent ELEVATION system mapped to layer importance, not a uniformly flat plane: create_instance native UIShadow on surfaces (set_property tuned BlurRadius/Offset/Spread/Transparency) so shadows grow softer/larger for higher layers — small soft on HUD, larger on panels, largest on modals — and/or use per-corner UICorner radii for distinctive shapes. The shadow size communicates which layer an element sits on.
steps.pitfalls: A uniformly flat z=0 UI with square corners (or duplicate-frame/9-slice shadow hacks) reads as generic. Uniform corner radius with no shadow/elevation language only reaches partial — map shadow size to importance across HUD/panel/modal tiers.

steps.instruction: Make resizable surfaces hold crisp corners and undistorted proportions under resize: for custom-art panels/buttons create_instance an ImageLabel/ImageButton and set_property ScaleType=Slice with a defined SliceCenter (the 3x3 divider) and SliceScale so corners stay crisp while edges stretch on one axis and the center fills (ScaleType=Tile to repeat textures). For Frame-based surfaces, size by Scale, hold proportion with a UIAspectRatioConstraint, and keep UICorner radius consistent across sizes.
steps.pitfalls: Stretching a button image warps its corners, and fixed-offset square frames distort/break on resize. Process icons with alpha-bleed to avoid edge halos; avoid baked-in shadows on sliced art that break when scaled.

steps.instruction: Wire TweenService micro-feedback as a SYSTEM, input-correct and scalable: run_luau a feedback module that, on MouseEnter, plays a snappy ~0.2s hover (scale-up via a CHILD UIScale and/or UIStroke 0->2-3px + brightness shift) and a press scale-down that settles; animate panel open/close by pre-setting the frame off-screen (Visible=true) and tweening Position in (Back ease overshoot), and add a Lighting blur on modal open. Make it auto-apply to runtime-spawned/templated elements via a PlayerGui.DescendantAdded linker (or bake it into reusable component templates) and bind interaction to button.Activated (mouse/touch/gamepad).
steps.pitfalls: Tweening Size on a layout-driven child fights the layout (tween a child UIScale instead); tweening UIStroke.Thickness on text re-rasterizes glyphs every frame (flicker + perf). Static buttons and blink-in menus are the clearest 'made in 10 minutes' tell. Feedback only on load-time buttons wired to mouse-only MouseButton1Click misses runtime-spawned cards and non-mouse input.

steps.instruction: Give the animation a deliberate, consistent PERSONALITY: in run_luau choose one easing family matched to the UI's tone (Sine/Quad Out for calm/premium, Back/Elastic for playful) and apply it consistently across ALL transitions via a shared TweenInfo, and stagger list/grid child reveals (a small incremental task.wait/delay per child) for a cascading entrance.
steps.pitfalls: No animation, or one undifferentiated default/linear tween with no tonal intent, fails this. A bare 'it has tweens' without a chosen tone-matched family only reaches partial.

steps.instruction:
Carry in-content emphasis through a system, not one flat treatment: set_property RichText=true on labels and embed inline tags in a single string (, , ,
) to color/weight parts of it — damage numbers, highlighted keywords, label-vs-value — escaping literal <>& and re-applying after localization. At minimum, apply the palette accent to the text that should stand out within your multi-tier weighted type scale.
steps.pitfalls: One default font size and one flat color on every label means nothing stands out. RichText markup is stripped by localization — re-apply after translating; unescaped < > & break the parse.

steps.instruction: Build stateful UI as reusable components separated from data: run_luau to define ONE component (a function/template taking props) reused with different props (one Menu/Card reused), with visibility/values driven by state and structure declarative — not duplicated hand-placed instances. Then decouple presentation from data: feed the components FROM data (one template instantiated per data item), and at full strength subscribe the UI to an external reactive store (e.g. Charm) with a view-state-vs-game-state boundary, driving continuous/per-frame animation through bindings (useBinding)/springs rather than state.
steps.pitfalls: Hand-placed duplicated instances per screen can't scale or stay consistent. Baking game data into static instances is the coupling that makes UI unmaintainable — render from data through a reusable template layer; keep UI-only view state (open menu, selected tab) in the component layer and game state (coins, inventory) in the store.

steps.instruction: Compose complex screens as a deliberate header/body/footer information system that steers the eye: create_instance a vertical composition (a framing header and footer Frame around a distinct body Frame, e.g. darker header/footer framing a lighter body) and add a stated eye-steering mechanism toward key info — color weight and/or UIGradient direction and/or a focal-flow — so the screen reads as a navigable information system rather than a flat undifferentiated grid.
steps.pitfalls: A flat undifferentiated hand-placed layout with default colors and no composition fails. Stating focal flow without a framing structure (or vice versa) only reaches partial — commit to both the header/body/footer framing AND the eye-steering mechanism. Close the loop with capture/capture_angles then evaluate(category='gui'), refining the lowest-scoring criteria first.
